rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results <U+2014> a 2-year outdoor pot experiment (Bari, Italy) on autumn-sown sugar beet under three drip irrigation frequencies (30, 50, 70% TAW depletion), with TDR soil moisture monitoring, root water uptake calculation (Table 3) and root length density at harvest (Table 4).
rows.notes: The study does not measure soil water tension at all (only volumetric moisture by TDR) and reports no -10 to -30 kPa range. It does not show that drip maintains stable root-zone water status; on the contrary Figure 3a shows soil moisture before irrigation close to wilting point in the top 0.2 m for all treatments and declining in deeper layers as the interval lengthened. What the study actually shows is that total daily root water uptake per plant was not significantly different among the three frequencies (1471 vs 1440-1410 mL/day) because plants shifted uptake to deeper layers (SWD3 took ~60% from 0.6-1.0 m) via acclimation of the root system (higher efficiency of deep roots, higher root/shoot ratio), not via buffered soil water tension. The experiment used surface drip lines in 1.3 m pots, one plant each, not subsurface drip or a field; no yield data. The review's mechanism claim (stable tension buffering interval effects) is therefore not a result of this study.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a pot experiment on root water uptake and root length density under three drip irrigation frequencies; it provides no tension measurements and attributes insensitivity of total uptake to root acclimation rather than to stable root-zone water status.
